correctness.rationale: For ellipsoid-uniform points, the difference of two standard-ball points factors into an independent radial variable and Haar direction. Direct ball-intersection integration gives each positive rational radial normalization. Squared Haar-direction coordinates are Dirichlet(1/2,...,1/2); their exact generating product yields the polynomial whose reciprocal roots are squared semiaxes. Constant-term perturbation of real-rooted monic polynomials proves sharp generic moment count. Rouché root-cluster comparison on bounded real-root spectra gives 1/d Hölder continuity, and an explicit two-family real-root perturbation near any ball makes the exponent optimal. Independent rational Cartesian moment expansions and exact coefficient inversions passed for dimensions 2-5; the proof covers every fixed d>=2. No claim is made about finite-sample inference.

originality.rationale: The closest accessible full-text geometric papers give forward mean-distance or full-covariogram-to-distance integrals, not the specified finite raw pair-distance moment inverse, generic minimality, or sharp stability. Classical spherical quadratic-form theory covers the angular factor and may conceal a prior equivalent; its full article remained inaccessible. The published central-section-volume inverse-moment result uses the same Dirichlet transform but a different measurement, with a determinant-dependent scaling not known before reconstructing axes; its complete published result was inspected and does not state pair-distance identification or optimal inverse Hölder stability. Current evidence supports originality provisionally, subject to the documented historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: Classical spherical-quadratic-form distribution formulas may implicitly contain finite-moment spectral reconstruction and require deeper historical checking.
The accessible indexed central-section-volume inverse theorem shares the Dirichlet algebra; its full text was read and establishes strong methodological overlap, though its measured quantity differs.
Forward pair-distance/covariogram identities are long-established; the originality claim is restricted to the exact geometric inverse cutoff and optimal stability exponent.

value.rationale: Recovering an ellipsoid from unoriented distances between uniform interior points is a natural geometric tomography problem. The result supplies an explicit dimension-d cutoff, a proof that d-1 cannot work at generic shapes, a constructive characteristic-polynomial inverse and an optimal 1/d Hölder modulus at the maximally symmetric shape. It is a self-contained inverse classification with an actionable exact-data procedure; the claim deliberately excludes statistical estimation and unsupported downstream uses.
